Radiology Division | 28 January 2025 | Multiparametric MRI Prostate

Clinical context: Follow-up on established prostate malignancy. Current PSA stands at 11.2 ng/mL, with a prior PI-RADS 5 lesion documented.

Protocol employed includes T2-weighted, diffusion-weighted, and dynamic contrast-enhanced imaging.

The gland measures 61.0 mL. On T2-weighted sequences, a discrete hypointense focus occupies the left peripheral zone near the base-mid transition, spanning roughly 18 × 15 × 12 mm. Diffusion mapping shows pronounced signal drop with matching ADC hypointensity, confirming restricted diffusion. Contrast kinetics demonstrate focal, early arterial enhancement within the target area. Capsular integrity remains intact without seminal vesicle involvement. Regional lymph nodes appear normal in size and structure.

Assessment highlights a PI-RADS 5 lesion in the left peripheral zone (base/mid), measuring approx. 18 mm.
PSA density: 0.18 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.8541575.
